summary.text: A 71-year-old woman with long-standing poorly controlled diabetes, uremia on regular hemodialysis and atherosclerosis of the lower extremities injured her left calf in a fall in July 2016. The 2nd toe of the left foot darkened and became tender, and after angiography with balloon dilatation and 2nd toe amputation her condition kept deteriorating until admission on October 23, 2017.

On admission the wound reached bone and involved the 1st to 3rd toes and two-thirds of the plantar area, with purulent secretions, a swollen foot and a lost dorsal artery undulation. Albumin was 24.3 g/L with electrolyte disturbances, fasting blood glucose was 14.5 mmol/L and postprandial blood glucose was 15.8 mmol/L. Culture grew Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Enterococcus faecium, and the case was classified as Wagner grade 4 diabetic foot with vascular occlusion.

Above-knee amputation was recommended but the family declined, so nutrition, electrolyte and circulation therapy, Sulperazon, nibbled debridement and semiclosure dressing therapy were used. The 3rd toe shed spontaneously on hospital day 19, the necrotic 1st toe was removed, and fibroblast growth factor was given. After systematic wound therapy and nursing care a fistula formed and was treated with low-pressure NPWT.

After 90 days of treatment the foot lesions healed and the fistula closed. No recurrence was detected during 6 months of follow-up, high position amputation was avoided, and the authors state that quality of life greatly improved.
